title: Precedent or Intent? What Coding Agents Follow When Evolving Existing Code
abstract: arXiv:2610.38244v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Existing code reveals past implementation decisions but rarely explains the reasoning behind them. When coding agents implement new features or modify existing functionality, past decisions may conflict with new task instructions. This raises a fundamental question for agentic software evolution: when multiple implementations satisfy the same functional requirements, how do coding agents decide whether to follow existing code or new task instructions? We investigate this question through bidirectional, controlled experiments in purpose-built repositories, followed by validation in real-world open-source repositories. Our approach isolates three competing sources of guidance: (1) agents' default preferences, (2) repository precedents, and (3) explicit task instructions. We conduct 5,625 trials across four coding agents and six implementation pairs, with validation in four open-source repositories spanning three programming languages. We

translated_title: 先例还是意图？编程代理在演进现有代码时遵循什么
translated_abstract: 现有代码揭示了过去的实现决策，但很少解释这些决策背后的推理过程。当编程代理实现新功能或修改现有功能时，过去的决策可能与新的任务指令发生冲突。这为代理式软件演进提出了一个根本性问题：当多种实现方式都能满足相同的功能需求时，编程代理如何决定是遵循现有代码还是遵循新的任务指令？我们通过在专门构建的代码仓库中进行双向对照实验来研究这一问题，随后在真实世界的开源仓库中进行验证。我们的方法隔离了三种相互竞争的指导来源：(1) 代理的默认偏好，(2) 仓库先例，以及 (3) 明确的任务指令。我们在四个编程代理和六个实现对上开展了5,625次试验，并在涵盖三种编程语言的四个开源仓库中进行了验证。
tldr: 该研究通过5,625次对照试验首次系统揭示了编程代理在演进现有代码时，如何在仓库先例、明确任务指令与自身默认偏好这三种相互竞争的指导来源之间做出抉择。
en_tdlr: This study systematically reveals, through 5,625 controlled trials validated in real-world open-source repositories, how coding agents decide among three competing sources of guidance—repository precedents, explicit task instructions, and their own default preferences—when evolving existing code.
